## Verbatim content capture

Elysia Tan Recipe — Judge's Summary

Overall Assessment: A high-extraction Kalita recipe designed specifically for dense washed coffees. It prioritises sweetness, body and balance over maximum clarity. Not a universal recipe—excellent when matched to the right coffee.

Core idea: Use an aggressive initial saturation (100g bloom) together with a coarse grind and high brew temperature (93°C) to maximise sugar extraction while maintaining an even extraction. The recipe intentionally trades a small amount of clarity for significantly higher sweetness and body.

Strengths: exceptional sweetness; heavy, syrupy mouthfeel; excellent balance between sweetness and acidity; wide, forgiving grind window; strong thermal stability throughout the brew; very repeatable due to minimal agitation.

Limitations: not recommended for natural coffees, anaerobic coffees, or very fresh coffees (<7 days). These coffees benefit from a smaller bloom and lower temperature.

Critical success factors:
- 100g bloom (5× dose): immediate full saturation; rapid heat transfer; maximum sugar extraction.
- 93°C; best suited for dense, high-altitude washed coffees.
- Coarse grind: Comandante 26–28 clicks.
- Pour structure: 100 → 200 → 250 → 320g. The large final pour restores slurry temperature and completes extraction without additional agitation.

Expected cup: very high sweetness; rounded malic acidity; heavy body; clean finish; low astringency; slightly reduced floral clarity compared to V60.

Target drawdown: 3:00–3:15. Beyond 3:30 risks over-extraction. Preheat stainless steel Kalita.

Adjustments: fresh coffee (<7 days), 80g bloom and 45s bloom time; washed Ethiopian, 91–92°C and 80g bloom; Kenya, 92°C and 90g bloom; natural/anaerobic, 89–90°C and 60g bloom.

The included judge opinion says the value is the combined design of aggressive saturation, coarse grinding, and thermal management—not a universal 93°C threshold or an inherently superior 100g bloom.
